# Exponential Models

## Cell expansion processes in cell and gene therapy

Cell expansion processes are common to most cell and gene therapy products, as you almost always start with fewer cells than you would like to use. The biological heart of a cellular expansion process is cellular division: one cell divides into two cells.

This then suggests a model we might use: exponential growth. And for these purposes, an exponential growth model will work well enough. This model multiplies a doubling time represented by $T_D$ by an elapsed time to calculate the number of doublings. The number of doublings is then multipled by your starting cell count $q_1$ to produce a final cell count $q_2$

$q_2 = q_1 * 2^{T_D * t_2 - t_1}$


```{r exponential-growth-data}
# Make a data frame containing two cell counts at two elapsed times
df_exponential_growth <- data.frame(
  cell_number = c(15000 , 98000),
  elapsed_time = c(12 , 192)
)
# Show the data frame
df_exponential_growth
```

```{r exponential-growth-plot}
df_exponential_growth |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = elapsed_time, y = cell_number)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
    labs(x = "Elapsed Time (hours)", y = "Cell Count")
```
